# Casts and type introspection.

=== string of integer
(string 42)
--- want
"42"

=== string of float
(string 1.5)
--- want
"1.5"

=== string of small float
(string 0.1)
--- want
"0.1"

=== string of large number uses exponent
(string 100000000000000000000)
--- want
"1e+20"

=== string switches to exponent form at a million
(string 1000000)
--- want
"1e+06"

=== string stays decimal below a million
(string 999999)
--- want
"999999"

=== string keeps fraction digits in exponent form
(string 1234567.8)
--- want
"1.2345678e+06"

=== string stays decimal down to ten-thousandths
(string 0.0001)
--- want
"0.0001"

=== string switches to exponent form below that
(string 0.00001)
--- want
"1e-05"

=== string of a negative number
(string -42.5)
--- want
"-42.5"

=== string of true
(string #t)
--- want
"#t"

=== string of false
(string #f)
--- want
"#f"

=== string passes through
(string "x")
--- want
"x"

=== string of list
(string (list 1 2))
--- want
"(list 1 2)"

=== string of nested list with string
(string (list "a" (list 2)))
--- want
"(list \"a\" (list 2))"

=== string of tuple
(string (tuple 1 2))
--- want
"(tuple 1 2)"

=== string of a function is an error
(string (fn (x) x))
--- error

=== string arity
(string)
--- error

=== number of numeric string
(number "1.5")
--- want
1.5

=== number trims whitespace
(number " 42 ")
--- want
42

=== number with exponent
(number "1e3")
--- want
1000

=== number with plus sign
(number "+5")
--- want
5

# The cast follows the host's numeric parser, unlike a source literal.
=== number accepts inf
(number "inf")
--- want
(/ 1e308 1e-308)

=== number accepts an underscore separator
(number "1_000")
--- want
1000

=== number rejects hex
(number "0x10")
--- error

=== number of a number
(number 7)
--- want
7

=== number of non-numeric string
(number "abc")
--- error

=== number of empty string
(number "")
--- error

=== number of malformed
(number "1.5.5")
--- error

=== number of a bool
(number #t)
--- error

=== cross-kind compare via string
(= (string 1) "1")
--- want
#t

=== cross-kind compare via number
(= (number "2") 2)
--- want
#t

=== type-of number
(type-of 1)
--- want
"number"

=== type-of string
(type-of "s")
--- want
"string"

=== type-of bool
(type-of #t)
--- want
"bool"

=== type-of list
(type-of (list 1))
--- want
"list"

=== type-of tuple
(type-of (tuple 1))
--- want
"tuple"

=== type-of function
(type-of (fn (x) x))
--- want
"func"

=== type-of arity
(type-of)
--- error

# Number text is exact both ways for every double, in every runtime and host:
# the shortest digits that read back, and reading rounds correctly however
# many digits there are. A host without a C library once held only to 15
# digits between 1e-8 and 1e22.

=== string of a 17-digit result
(string (+ 0.1 0.2))
--- want
"0.30000000000000004"

=== string of a huge number
(string 1e300)
--- want
"1e+300"

=== string of the smallest subnormal
(string 5e-324)
--- want
"5e-324"

=== string of the largest double
(string 1.7976931348623157e308)
--- want
"1.7976931348623157e+308"

=== string of the smallest normal
(string 2.2250738585072014e-308)
--- want
"2.2250738585072014e-308"

=== a 17-digit literal reads as the nearest double
(= 9.9999999999999995e-08 1e-7)
--- want
#t

=== number reads past twenty zeros after the point
(= (number "0.0000000000000000000001") 1e-22)
--- want
#t

=== number underflows to zero
(number "1e-400")
--- want
0

=== number rounds just above half the smallest subnormal up
(= (number "2.4703282292062328e-324") 5e-324)
--- want
#t

=== number of thirty digits
(string (number "123456789012345678901234567890"))
--- want
"1.2345678901234568e+29"
